sourceNotes: Values are approximate representative placeholders for ruleset tuning, not a clinical nutrient database.

sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 1.6 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 0.2 grams, supporting a cleaner fat profile. Omega 3 is 50 milligrams, not adding much omega 3. For grains, fat usually matters less than the carb score.
sections.subtitleText: 1.6g of fat. Saturated fat is 0.2g, supporting a cleaner fat profile. Omega 3 is 50mg, not adding much omega 3. For grains, fat usually matters less than the carb score.

sections.title: Carbs
sections.narration: 75.9 grams of carbs. Fibre is 15.1 grams, helping with digestion and steadier meals. Starch is 57 grams, supporting useful staple-carb energy, and it is still a strong secondary mark. For grains, carb quality matters much more than the raw number.

sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: Positives first: can keep meals cheap and steady. That is a genuine category strength. Usually affordable and scalable. Practicality matters for staple foods. Easy to batch cook at scale. That practicality is part of why grains matter.

closing.summary: Big strengths are fibre, protein, and magnesium, but the biggest weaknesses are low vitamin E, low calcium, and low omega 3. It's good for digestion, heart health, and energy and endurance sports because fibre helps digestion and keeps meals steadier, fibre is useful for heart health, and the carb section gives usable fuel.
